title: Go SDK streaming: session grace, deadline semantics, and reconnect/backoff guidance
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Go SDK streaming sessions currently expose context cancellation directly to the underlying transport which can cause abrupt stream termination, partial events to be lost, and confusion for application authors about whether to retry. Goal: define well-scoped semantics and ergonomic APIs for graceful session shutdown, cancelation grace periods, and deterministic reconnect/backoff behavior so clients can build resilient features without custom wiring.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a documented high-level API for session shutdown that supports a configurable grace period (e.g., StreamWithGrace(ctx, grace time.Duration)).

When parent context is canceled, SDK will attempt to drain in-flight responses and send a clean end-of-stream signal within the grace period; if grace expires, session closes and returns context.Canceled to caller.

Reconnect policy exposed via options: RetryNever | RetryImmediate | RetryWithBackoff (with jitter). Default: RetryWithBackoff for transient network errors, no retry for server-initiated rejections (4xx).
No breaking changes to existing stream API; opt-in via new factory options.
Unit + integration tests covering cancel during streaming, graceful drain, and retries under simulated network errors.
design_decisions: Do not rely solely on parent context cancellation — expose an explicit StreamClose/Grace API so callers can choose between immediate abort and cooperative shutdown.
Grace period is advisory: SDK will attempt to gracefully close but must honor global timeouts. The effective deadline = min(parent deadline, start + grace).
Reconnect/backoff policy is pluggable; provide sane default (exponential backoff, initial 200ms, max 5s, ±20% jitter) and metrics hooks so Console can show retry counts and cost impact.
Avoid implicit buffering of large message queues on client side; provide a small bounded buffer (default 8 messages) and expose config for advanced users.
implementation_notes: API additions: StreamOptions{GracePeriod time.Duration, ReconnectPolicy string, BufferCapacity int}. Add functional option helpers: WithStreamGrace(time.Duration), WithReconnectPolicy("backoff"), WithBufferCapacity(n).

Behavior on ctx cancel: spawn a shutdown goroutine that attempts to read remaining messages for up to GracePeriod, then call transport.Close(). Return a wrapped error that annotates whether the close was graceful or forced.
Reconnect classification: network errors (net.Error temporary || io.EOF from transport) => eligible for retry; protocol errors (400/401/403) => no retry. Attach HTTP status in stream error metadata.
Error surface: add helpers IsGracefulClose(err error) and IsTransientStreamError(err error) so callers can decide higher-level retries.
testing_plan: Unit tests: simulate parent ctx cancellation at different points (before first frame, mid-stream, while draining) and assert returned error and metrics (graceUsed=true/false).

Integration tests (ci-network): flaky network simulator that injects delays and connection resets. Validate reconnect counts and ensure no message duplication when server provides monotonically increasing sequence numbers.
Chaos test: orchestrate forced process kill of SDK client to ensure server-side sessions expire cleanly (coord with server team).
Bench: measure latency/throughput with default buffer capacity 8 vs 0 and with grace enabled vs disabled to quantify cost/latency trade-off.
rollout_plan: Feature behind opt-in flag in v0.26.0 experimental API.
Merge small change with feature gate, run full e2e, and dogfood in internal Console integrations.
After 2 weeks of dogfooding and no major regressions, flip default ReconnectPolicy to backoff in v0.27.0 and announce SDK behavioral changes in changelog with migration guidance.
Dashboard: add telemetry for stream_close_type (graceful|forced) and retry_count per-session.
